verdict.rationale: Bento is an agent observability platform, not an agent itself, so an official MCP server is a fair question. The quickstart says that after installing the skill, each coding tool 'loads the docs over MCP', which points to a first-party MCP endpoint serving documentation. Nothing shows an MCP server exposing Bento's product data or actions (traces, issues, signals); those are documented only through the CLI. missing for 10: a documented MCP server endpoint and install config, MCP tools for product operations (runs, signals, issues), auth details, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect an agent via an official MCP server

citations.quote: Each tool installs the skill the same way, then loads the docs over MCP.
Paste this into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, or Windsurf. It installs Bento’s Agent Skills and hands the agent the full integration playbook
